novel_features.name: Construction Leads
novel_features.description: Get a contactable outreach list of companies that just won construction contracts: one row per winner with email, phone, city and VAT/HRB id when TED reports them, plus contract value and what is being built.
novel_features.rationale: TED lists contacts in a different order than winner names; only a local zip against the tenderer list plus seen-state turns award notices into deduplicated, callable leads.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs sales leads from public contract awards instead of raw notices.

novel_features.name: Open-tender ranker
novel_features.description: Rank open tenders by deadline urgency, contract value and keyword fit into a prioritized bid shortlist.
novel_features.rationale: Combines three signals over every open call in the local corpus; TED and existing tools sort by one column only.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it when asked which open tenders are worth bidding on this week.

novel_features.name: Buyer dossier
novel_features.description: Profile a contracting authority: publishing cadence, CPV mix, typical contract values and repeat winners.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining years of an authority's calls and awards, which only exists together in the synced store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it before bidding to one authority or when investigating its award history.

novel_features.name: Market concentration
novel_features.description: See which companies capture what share of awarded value in a sector and country, with an HHI concentration score.
novel_features.rationale: The API has no aggregation; share and HHI need every award in the slice grouped by winner name and country.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to answer who dominates a procurement market.

novel_features.name: Winner dossier
novel_features.description: Profile one company that wins public contracts: win timeline, total value, buyers, regions and latest contact data.
novel_features.rationale: Aggregates every award row for a company across years, which no TED view or API call provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it before calling a lead or sizing up a competitor.

novel_features.name: Tender incumbents
novel_features.description: For one open tender, see who previously won contracts from the same buyer in the same category.
novel_features.rationale: Joins the open call's buyer and CPV prefix against historical awards in the local store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to judge your odds against the incumbent before writing a proposal.

novel_features.name: Deadline heat
novel_features.description: A ranked list of tenders closing within days, weighted by urgency, value and how few companies usually win this buyer's awards.
novel_features.rationale: Competition comes from the historical number of distinct winners per award for the same buyer or CPV division in the local store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it for last-minute bid triage.

novel_features.name: Buyer award rate
novel_features.description: See per buyer how many calls for tender end in published awards and how many distinct companies win.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining call notices to award notices per buyer, which the API cannot do.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to compare buyers by openness before targeting them.

novel_features.name: Dark buyers
novel_features.description: Flag contracting authorities whose tenders rarely produce public awards or keep going to one company.
novel_features.rationale: Applies award-rate and winner-diversity thresholds over the per-buyer call/award join.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it for procurement integrity screening; results are heuristic signals, not findings.

novel_features.name: Procurement velocity
novel_features.description: See whether a procurement market is heating up or cooling off with weekly notice counts versus the same window last year.
novel_features.rationale: Time-series bucketing over the synced corpus; no single API call returns trends.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to spot demand shifts in a sector.

novel_features.name: CPV drift
novel_features.description: See which procurement categories grow or shrink year over year in a country's spending mix.
novel_features.rationale: Year-over-year pivot of the full historical corpus held locally.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it for market sizing and policy research.

narrative.headline: The EU public procurement corpus searchable offline, with contactable leads from contract award winners.
narrative.value_prop: Sync TED notices into a local SQLite store and turn award notices into outreach lists with leads, including email, phone and VAT id per winner when TED reports them. Rank open calls with score and deadline-heat, and analyze markets with concentration, buyer, winner, velocity and cpv-drift. No API key needed.

quickstart.comment: Check config, paths and TED API reachability
Pull the last 30 days of German construction notices into the local store
List companies that just won construction contracts, with contact data
Rank open tenders worth bidding on

troubleshoots.fix: Run eu-tenders-pp-cli sync --since 90d --param country=DEU --param cpv=45 first; they read the local store

troubleshoots.symptom: Lead titles look like reference codes
troubleshoots.fix: Re-run eu-tenders-pp-cli sync for that window; sync stores the procedure title (title-proc) ahead of lot reference titles
Run eu-tenders-pp-cli fields to check field names; values with spaces need quotes

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI to find EU public tenders, analyze who wins public contracts, or build B2B lead lists from contract award winners. It suits recurring sales prospecting, bid triage and procurement market research over TED data.
anti_triggers: Submitting or publishing notices to TED as an eSender
National below-threshold tenders that are not published on TED
